subject: physics
question_text: Why do liquids have no linear and areal expansions?

mark_split.label: A liquid has no fixed shape

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2019 (Q8) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced from that paper. Physics hand-checked: a liquid has a definite volume but no definite shape, so it has no length and no surface area of its own to expand; only cubical expansion, ΔV = γV₀Δθ, is defined for it, and the relations β = 2α and γ = 3α belong to solids.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: A liquid has no fixed shape
lines: A liquid has no shape of its own. It takes
the shape of the vessel that holds it.
So a liquid has no definite length and no
definite surface area of its own.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say that a liquid has no shape of its own.
steps.why: Linear expansion needs a definite length and areal expansion needs a definite surface, and a liquid supplies neither because it flows into the shape of its container.
common_mistakes: Saying that liquids do not expand at all. They do expand, but only in volume.

recall.must_convey: That a liquid has no shape of its own, so it has no definite length or area.
accept: takes the shape of the vessel

steps.memory_tip: No fixed shape means no fixed length and no fixed area to measure.

steps.label: Only cubical expansion
lines: A liquid does have a definite volume, so
only its change in volume can be measured.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name cubical, or volume, expansion as the only kind.
steps.why: Volume is the one dimension a liquid keeps, so the coefficient of cubical expansion γ is the only expansion coefficient a liquid can have.
common_mistakes: Writing β = 2α and γ = 3α for a liquid. Those relations hold for solids.

recall.must_convey: That a liquid has a definite volume, so only cubical expansion is defined for it.
reject: takes the shape of the vessel

steps.memory_tip: A liquid keeps one definite thing, its volume. So only γ is defined for it.

insider_note: Two marks — no definite shape, therefore only volume expansion. Naming cubical expansion by name is what earns the second.
